entities.summary:
JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an American multinational investment bank and financial services company with roots tracing to 1799. Today it is the largest bank in the United States and one of the world's largest financial institutions by assets, operating across investment banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing, asset management, and private banking.

The bank's lineage combines J.P. Morgan & Co., founded by financier J.P. Morgan who stabilized the US financial system during the Panics of 1893 and 1907, with Chase Manhattan Bank, Bank One, and Bear Stearns. J.P. Morgan personally arranged the bailout of US banks during the 1907 financial panic, a role later institutionalized in the Federal Reserve. The modern JPMorgan Chase emerged from the 2000 merger of Chase Manhattan and J.P. Morgan & Co.

Under CEO Jamie Dimon from 2005, JPMorgan Chase navigated the 2008 financial crisis relatively well, acquiring failed Bear Stearns and Washington Mutual with government assistance. With over $3.7 trillion in assets and operations in 100+ countries, it finances governments, corporations, and individuals. Its investment bank consistently ranks first or second globally in M&A advisory, equity underwriting, and bond issuance.
